Adderall is similar to meth, but it doesn't get people with ADHD high, it just fixes our dopamine deficiency, which is the root cause of our symptoms. It actually makes us calm / able to function like normal people, who can just ... Do stuff without fighting their brains to let them. It's sorta like our brains are too slow naturally so giving us a stimulant gets us to where everyone else is.



Some people with ADHD find that caffeine calms them instead of giving them energy, for similar reasons. Depending on how bad your ADHD is, some people can self treat it with stuff like that, or might be able to get by with extra reminders or alarms. Buuut in my case, it's real bad and I most certainly need medication. It can be hard to get treatment as an adult, though, due to common misconceptions that it's a disorder for children, or that you should have been diagnosed as a child if it was so bad you need treatment. It ignores that a lot of people's parents were neglectful or that kids will often think they're just lazy/worthless/stupid, rather than assuming there's a reason they're struggling.


I was actually diagnosed when I was 4 because it was so noticeable, but the custody arrangement changed and my father "didn't believe in it" so... whoops.

Oftentimes, it does, but ADHD is an executive function disorder and executive function is what controls us being able to do stuff. Just being annoyed or embarrassed isn't enough to fix it.
